title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. \hat\Pi_{0,3} is the profinite group attached to P^1 minus {0,1,∞} with its symmetries. The generators are sigma_infty and rho, where rho is the order-3 rotation; the next page shows l_0, l_1 mapping to (1 -2;0 1) and (1 0;-2 1), the standard generators of Gamma(2). There is a 'congruence' map x ↦ x̲ from \hat\Pi_{0,3} to SL(2,Ẑ).

The group M_{0,3}^{!~}[0] is Grothendieck's group of solutions of the 'équation des lacets'. Its elements u = u_{ξ,η} act on \hat\Pi_{0,3} by ρ ↦ ξρξ^{-1} and σ_∞ ↦ ησ_∞η^{-1}. It is a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group, but it contains inner-type elements such as L_0 = <l_0>. Each u has an image u̲ in GL(2,Ẑ), and the previous page shows u̲ is upper triangular, (μ M;0 1), with μ invertible. The map is compatible with the action: underline(u(x)) = u̲ x̲ u̲^{-1} (166). The composition law in the group is ξ'' = u'(ξ)ξ', which after reduction gives (167): ξ̲'' = int(u̲')(ξ̲)·ξ̲'.

Theorem (165). u ↦ u̲ is a group homomorphism. By (163bis), ξ̲ and u̲ determine each other, so the theorem reduces to the following statement on this page. Let B ⊂ GL(2,Ẑ) be the 'Borel' group {(μ M;0 1)} (169). Define F: B → SL(2,Ẑ) by F(u̲) = μ^{-1}·[u̲,ρ], where [u̲,ρ] = u̲ ρ(u̲)^{-1} = u̲ρu̲^{-1}ρ^{-1}. Then F is a 1-cocycle for the conjugation action (171): F(u̲'u̲) = int(u̲')(F(u̲))·F(u̲').

This is the standard identity for commutators, [u'u,ρ] = u'[u,ρ]u'^{-1}·[u',ρ], together with multiplicativity of det. Combined with injectivity of u̲ ↦ ξ̲, the cocycle identity (171) turns (167) into u̲_{ξ''} = u̲_{ξ'}u̲_ξ, which is (168).

Corollary (172). The full group M_{0,3}^{!~} is the semidirect product M_{0,3}^{!~}[0]·\hat𝔖^→_{0,3}, where \hat𝔖 is the group of permutation symmetries. Sending u_ξ·a ↦ (u̲_ξ)'·a̲ gives a homomorphism to GL(2,Ẑ)' = GL(2,Ẑ)/±1, using (163).

Purpose. This attaches a simple adelic invariant (μ, M) in a Borel subgroup to each element of the lacets group. The invariant is the cyclotomic-type character μ together with a translation part M. On the next page it is used to coordinatize the pairs (ξ,η) via ξ = [u̲,ρ], η = [u̲,σ_∞], and to study the quotient by L_0, which acts by M ↦ M - 2n.

The oblique left margin seems to note a defect. Defining M_{0,3}^!(o) requires a base point, and its intersection with the inner part is L_0 ≠ {1}. A better-normalized subgroup would be desirable.
errors: Determinant bookkeeping in (170) looks inconsistent as transcribed. [u̲,ρ] = u̲ρu̲^{-1}ρ^{-1} is a commutator, so it already has det 1. Multiplying by the scalar μ^{-1} gives det μ^{-2}, not 1, so F would not land in SL(2,Ẑ). Either the factor (det u̲)^{-1} is meant differently (e.g. a twisted action of ρ, or work mod ±1), or it is a leftover from the struck-out formula. The cocycle identity itself is unaffected, since a multiplicative central factor preserves it.
The reduction from (167) to (168) silently uses injectivity of u̲ ↦ ξ̲ = F(u̲) (163bis), which is cited but not reproved here.
The corollary passes to GL(2,Ẑ)/±1 without explaining here why the ±1 ambiguity arises. It presumably comes from lifting the elements a of \hat𝔖_{0,3} (cf. previous page's NB).

ideas.what: Congruence/adelic image of an element of a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group in a Borel subgroup of GL(2,Ẑ): u ↦ (μ M;0 1), shown to be a homomorphism
ideas.modern_name: Image of GT-hat (or G_Q) acting on \hat F_2 ⊂ \hat{SL_2(Z)}, read through the congruence quotient SL_2(Ẑ); cyclotomic character plus a translation/Kummer-type component
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cyclotomic character λ of GT-hat: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; actions on \hat{SL_2(Z)} and Gamma(2): Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Ihara (1990s)
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or La Longue Marche as far as known; these are the unpublished 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' (cote 140-3)

ideas.what: Reformulation of the homomorphism property as a 1-cocycle identity for the commutator map u ↦ [u,ρ] = uρu^{-1}ρ^{-1} on the Borel B
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian 1-cocycle (crossed homomorphism) given by a coboundary-type commutator

ideas.what: Extension of the homomorphism to the semidirect product with the symmetric-group part \hat𝔖_{0,3}, landing in GL(2,Ẑ)/±1
ideas.modern_name: Extended GT / action of S_3 symmetries of P^1 - {0,1,∞} (orbifold PSL_2(Z) level)
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche discusses \hat Π_{0,3} with the symmetric group action, but not this specific homomorphism

missed.claim: Grothendieck's own (unpublished) parametrization of elements of his lacets group by an adelic Borel matrix (μ M;0 1), with ξ = [u̲,ρ], η = [u̲,σ_∞]. The 'translation' coordinate M records inner/base-point (L_0) data, as in M ↦ M - 2n on the next page. This is an explicit, independent precursor-style treatment of the GT-hat congruence image. It is not new mathematically but is absent from the published record of his work.
missed.quote: F_ξ(u̲'u̲) = int(u̲')(F_ξ(u̲)).F_ξ(u̲') ... L'application M_{0,3}^{!~} = M_{0,3}^{!~}[0].\hat𝔖_{0,3} → GL(2,Ẑ)' est homomorphisme de groupes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents how Grothendieck handled the base-point / inner-automorphism issue (M_{0,3}^!(o) ∩ inner = L_0 ≠ {1}) in his version of GT. That issue later reappears in groupoid/tangential-base-point treatments of GT.

missed.claim: Margin note proposing to replace M_{0,3}^!(o) by a better-normalized subgroup avoiding the nontrivial intersection L_0. This thread is not completed on this page.
missed.quote: cela tient au fait que pour définir M_{0,3}(o) ... L_0 ≠ {1} il serait utile ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It corresponds to the choice of normalization (f in the commutator subgroup, tangential base points) that Drinfeld/Ihara made. It is of historical rather than mathematical novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine verification: a commutator-cocycle identity and a homomorphism to a Borel subgroup of GL(2,Ẑ)/±1, within Grothendieck's unpublished GT-type development. Historically interesting as his own setup, but the mathematics is elementary and parallels known GT-hat results.
transcription_corrections: 'Par multiplicativité de det, on se ramène [-(u, u' ∈ B)-] : où ρ ...[?]' should read roughly 'Par multiplicativité de det, on se ramène [-(u,u'∈B)-] à voir que u ↦ [u,ρ] = u ρ(u)^{-1} satisfait la relation des cocycles, ce qui est trivial.'

Left oblique margin: a plausible reading includes 'M_{0,3}^!(o) ∩ ... = L_0 ≠ {1}' rather than 'ξ_0 ≠ {ξ}', followed by 'il faudrait/il serait utile ... de façon que ...'. The reading remains uncertain.
Top line: '(163 bis)' is written over the line end, 'Comme ξ et u̲ = u_ξ se déterminent mutuellement (163 bis) il revient au même de dire'.
In (170) the struck-out material after (det u̲)^{-1} appears to be 'u̲^{-1}...ρ^{-1}(det u̲)^{-1}' with a further deleted '(μ^{-1}=...)'. The surviving formula is (det u̲)^{-1} [u̲,ρ].
